# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 43 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 11, Part 2 — Signs of the True and False Prophet

**43:1** "Hear now both the spirit of the divine and the spirit of earthly origin, and discern each one by means of his works. Trust the spirit that comes from above, from the power of God; but the earthly spirit has no power, is empty, and is foolish."

**43:2** "First, concerning the man who seems to have the Spirit: the one who exalts himself and desires the seat of honor and is bold and shameless and loquacious and lives in luxury and in many other deceptions — and who accepts payment for his prophesying, and if he does not receive it he will not prophesy — can the Spirit of God receive payment for prophesying? It is impossible for a prophet of God to do this. The spirit of such prophets, therefore, is earthly."

**43:3** "On the other hand, observe the character of the man who has the divine Spirit. The man who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble and keeps himself from all wickedness and the empty desire of this age, and makes himself more lowly than all men, and does not respond when asked a question, and does not speak of himself alone — for the Holy Spirit does not speak when a man wishes to speak, but speaks at the time when God wills him to speak."

**43:4** "When therefore the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the Holy Spirit, and prayer is made, the man is filled with the Holy Spirit and speaks to the congregation as God wills. In this way the Spirit of God will be made manifest. Such is the power of the Spirit of the Lord."

**43:5** "Hear now also concerning the earthly and empty spirit, which has no power but is foolish. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and seeks the first place, and is bold and shameless and loquacious and accustomed to luxury and many other deceits, and he accepts payment for his divination. When you see such a man, keep away from him."

**43:6** "Now hear again concerning the true prophet. The man who has the divine Spirit does not exalt himself or desire to speak first, nor does he live in luxury, nor does he make inquiry for money — but rather, if anyone inquires of him, he does not answer of himself but only by the will of God. And since the Holy Spirit of God himself rests upon this man, he speaks the things that the Lord commands."

**43:7** "When, therefore, both spirits come together in the same place, and if you wish — by means of prayer and supplication for discernment — to test which is true and which is false: first, test the man who has the divine Spirit through his way of life. See whether the life of the man who has the spirit is consistent with an upright and virtuous manner of living."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and precision in prophetic discernment vocabulary.*
